proposal.utterance: Classify 'the 2026 trial of X vs. Y'.

entities.label: 2026TrialXvsY
entities.rationale: A specific trial is a particular legal proceeding that unfolds in time — it has temporal parts (opening, examination, verdict), involves participants, and occurs at a definite spatiotemporal location. BFO Process (BFO_0000015) is the correct type for any occurring, temporally extended happening. This is a named individual because 'the 2026 trial of X vs. Y' refers to a specific, historically unique event.

entities.label: Trial
entities.rationale: The kind 'Trial' is a process class — a subclass of BFO Process — under which individual trials like 2026TrialXvsY are typed. Minting this class is appropriate because no existing working class represents legal trial proceedings.

entities.label: Year2026
entities.rationale: The year 2026 is a specific one-dimensional temporal region (BFO_0000038, subclass of BFO_0000008 Temporal Region). It is an individual because it denotes a uniquely identified calendar year, and is needed to ground the temporal indexing of the trial.

relations.rationale: The individual 2026TrialXvsY is an instance of the class Trial.
Trial is a subclass of BFO Process, since all trials are temporally extended occurrents.
BFO_0000132 (occurrent part of temporal region / 'occurs in') grounds the trial in its temporal region, the year 2026. This uses the BFO relation for situating a process within a temporal region.

open_questions: Who are X and Y? Are they individuals (natural persons) or institutional parties (corporations, states)? Their typing will determine what roles (e.g., LegalRight, LegalObligation, CourtAuthority bearers) they bear in this process.
Should 'Trial' be further specialized (e.g., CivilTrial, CriminalTrial, AppellateTrial)? The 'vs.' notation suggests civil or adversarial proceedings, but clarification would improve precision.
Is there a specific court or jurisdiction in which this trial occurs? If so, that would be a Site (BFO_0000029) individual that the trial is spatially located in.
Should the trial be linked to any existing working individuals (e.g., a specific LegalInstitution or Statute) already in the ontology?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'the 2026 trial of X vs. Y' picks out a specific, historically individuated legal proceeding. In BFO terms, any particular trial is a Process (BFO_0000015): it unfolds in time, has temporal parts, and involves participants. I mint the individual working:2026TrialXvsY typed under a new class working:Trial (itself a subclass of BFO_0000015), because no existing working class captures legal trial proceedings. The year 2026 is encoded as a one-dimensional temporal region individual (BFO_0000038) to ground the temporal indexing. The parties X and Y are not further typed here because the utterance does not specify their natures; open questions are raised for the user. No existing working individuals or classes are reused because none directly represent trials or their temporal grounding.
